name: Materials Science & Engr (Eng)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
A student wishing to enter the Engineer program must have completed the MS in Materials Science and Engineering requirements and must file a petition requesting admission to the program, stating the type of research to be done and the proposed supervising professor. Once approved, the Application for Candidacy must be submitted to the department’s student services director by the end of the second quarter in the Engineer program. Final changes in the Application for Candidacy form must be submitted no later than one academic quarter before degree conferral.
The 90-unit program must include nine units of graduate courses in Materials Science with a MATSCI subject code (no research units, seminars, colloquia, and MATSCI400 Participation in Materials Science Teaching, Participation in Teaching) beyond the requirements for the MS degree and additional research or other units to meet the 90-unit university minimum requirement. A grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 must be maintained for all degree coursework taken at Stanford.
The Engineer thesis must be approved and signed off by two Academic Council faculty members; one must be a MATSCI faculty member.
rules.notes: Graduate Degrees describes university requirements for the Engineer degree.

rules.name: MATSCI Elective Courses (three courses, 9 units)
rules.desc:
Beyond the requirements of the MS Program, an additional nine units of graduate courses in the MATSCI subject code must be completed.
Three MATSCI Elective Courses are required (9 units). These must be 200+ Level MATSCI Courses taken for a letter grade (seminars, labs, and research units cannot apply).
Earn at least 9 credits

rules.name: MS in Materials Science and Engineering requirements completed
Application for Candidacy by the end of the second quarter
3.0 GPA in all degree coursework at Stanford
Engineer thesis approved by two Academic Council faculty (one MATSCI)

gpa: Overall GPA of 3.0 for courses applied towards degree requirements.
grading: The minimum grade in each course applied towards degree requirements is a C. Students with a C- or below must re-take the course or satisfactorily complete an allowable replacement course.
transferPolicy: Refer to the University policy on Graduate Residency Transfer Credit
reviewNotes: The audit checks 90 units of graduate coursework, a C or better in each course, and three letter-graded MATSCI elective courses numbered 200 or above for 9 units (no seminars, labs or research units). Checked by hand: finishing the MS in Materials Science and Engineering requirements first, the Application for Candidacy by your second quarter, the 3.0 GPA, and the Engineer thesis approved by two faculty readers.
